newsitem.title: JAPAN: Scrapping of Japan Development Bank 'severe'-- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Scrapping of Japan Development Bank 'severe'-- MOF.

text.p: The decision to abolish the Japan Development Bank (JDB) is a very "severe and hard" one, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said on Monday.
"It is a very severe and a hard conclusion for us," Ogawa said, adding that the JDB was functioning at the moment and that there were people working for the bank.
He said no details, including the time frame for closing the JDB, had been set yet.
Earlier on Monday, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said the government planned to abolish the JDB as part of its overall administrative reform.
Mitsuzuka said he came to the decision after talks with a key official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's (LDP) task force on administrative reform.
The JDB is a government-affiliated body which makes long-term loans at low rates to the private sector, mainly for domestic infrastructure projects.
The streamlining of government-affiliated financial institutions had been at the core of discussions by the LDP's task force.
